beats.direction: Use the recurring witness with an on-screen disclaimer: CITY CONTEXT / NOT DAY-SPECIFIC.
beats.voice: Copenhagen turns participation into an evidence problem: admission, time, teardown, rights, screening, product data and institutional memory each demand a record. This chapter follows capture: The collection walks once; cameras, edits, metadata and rights agreements decide which view can be repeated and who can repeat it.
beats.onScreen: Then: Current CPHFW terms require show-production measures including waste sorting, avoidance of single-use backstage plastic and zero-waste set design under the framework’s stated definition.
beats.credit: Scandinavian Academy of Fashion Design · CC BY-SA 4.0

beats.direction: Animate only line reveals and state changes in the original evidence diagram.
beats.voice: Current CPHFW terms require show-production measures including waste sorting, avoidance of single-use backstage plastic and zero-waste set design under the framework’s stated definition. That earlier record fixes a point in time; it does not prove an inevitable progression toward the present.
beats.onScreen: Now: The terms permit a CPHFW representative to review backstage compliance on show day and allow additional documentation within a month; this is an operational evidence path, not an independent environmental audit.
beats.credit: Graphic © Rayven-Nikkita Collins; sources in claim ledger

beats.direction: Animate only line reveals and state changes in the original evidence diagram.
beats.voice: The distinction is material. A polished interface can survive after its workers, contracts, specifications or permission trail disappear, leaving the audience with an outcome but not its operating history.
beats.onScreen: Next: Show-level material inventories, energy use, transport boundaries, carbon calculations, suppliers and teardown outcomes remain unavailable unless brands or producers release them.
